The brown fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern list-bullet aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as brown coded rather than literal square-shape-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🟫 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate list-bullet energy. A partner sends it on a 'brown 🟫' list-bullet marker. A friend sends it on a 'square-pulse pulse 🟫' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'brown coded 🟫' list thread. The brown fill cue is what makes the emoji feel brown coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'brown coded square-shape moment.'

What separates 🟫 from the rest of the shape family is the brown register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'brown coded square-shape,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why 🟫 travels especially well on partner list-bullet markers, list-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with brown energy.
